content.text: The corpus does not contain the Act's definition of "personal data" or any scope provision, so I can't confirm from it whether the DPDP Rules 2025 reach a tool holding only room names and time slots. The Rules I retrieved (Rule 2) only say that undefined terms take their meaning from the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, and the obligations I found (Rules 9, 10, 11, 14) are framed around processing a Data Principal's personal data. On that basis, a tool with no personal data would likely fall outside them, but you should check the Act's definition of personal data (s. 2(t)) and its scope provision before relying on that, and note that room-booking records can become personal data if they are linked to an identifiable employee.

2. Definitions. — (1) In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires, –
(a) “Act” means the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 (22 of 2023);
(b) “techno-legal measures” means as referred to under rules 20 and 22;
(c) “user account” means the online account registered by the Data Principal with the Data Fiduciary, and
includes any profiles, pages, handles, email address, mobile number and other similar presences by means
of which such Data Principal is able to access the services of such Data Fiduciary; and
(d) “verifiable consent” means a consent as specified in rule 10 or 11.
(2) The words and expressions used in these rules and not defined, but defined in the Act, shall have the
same meanings respectively assigned to them in the Act.
